subject: Acme Bank eval setup & next steps — recommended models and dataset format
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@acmebank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-12T15:23:00Z
Subject: Acme Bank eval setup & next steps — recommended models and dataset format

Hi Erin —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation and super helpful context on the fraud-review and case-summarization flows. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we heard:
- Primary goal: reduce reviewer time on fraud alerts by surfacing high-quality case summaries and recommended actions (semi-structured).
- Target latency: sub-500ms median for single-turn generation at 2k token context for the UI path.
- Quality bar: human eval pass-rate >= 85% on relevancy + accuracy composite.

Redwood recommended models for initial eval (balance of cost, quality):
1) redwood/rodeo-13b-v2 (production baseline — strong quality/cost tradeoff)
2) redwood/rodeo-3b-quant (lower-cost variant for burst/quick responses)
3) open/llama2-70b (if you want to test highest-quality open model; expect higher cost and latency)

Benchmarks & prompt sets:
- Per-model perf/latency: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/rodeo-13b
- Example prompt set + eval harness (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cEvalPromptSets

Dataset format & required columns for the eval (we can accept CSV or JSONL):
- CSV recommended for initial handoff with header row. Required columns: input, reference, metadata
  - input: raw prompt/context (string)
  - reference: ground-truth summary/action (string)
  - metadata: JSON-stringified small object (agent_id, source_type, timestamp) — if you cannot provide JSON in a cell, include minimal text tags.
- File sizing guidance: up to 10k rows is fine; for initial run we recommend a stratified sample of 500-1,000 examples with at least 200 labeled critical cases.

Scoring criteria (initial plan):
- Automated metrics: ROUGE-L for abstractive summary overlap, BLEU for short action phrases, and embedding-similarity (cosine) threshold >= 0.80 using Redwood embeddings for semantic match.
- Human spot-check: random sample of 200 examples, reviewer scoring on 1-5 scale for correctness and hallucination risk.
- Pass threshold: composite score >= 0.85 (weighted: 60% automated, 40% human).

Security & hosting options:
- Hosted sandbox (shared infra, logs retained per our standard policy) — fastest to start.
- Private VPC eval (recommended if you need stricter controls): private evaluation instances, data stays in your VPC, KMS-managed keys.

Next steps:
1) Share a sample CSV (500 rows ideal) and indicate whether you prefer hosted sandbox or private VPC eval.
2) Rishi (cc'd) will coordinate the technical onboarding and run the baseline eval within 48 hours of receiving data.
3) We'll deliver a results deck and per-model recommendations within 5 business days of run completion.

I've attached a Redwood eval template (redwood-eval-template.jsonl) and a CSV sample to make the handoff easier.

If this looks good I can loop in our procurement contact for SLA/pricing (I attached the latest SLA/pricing doc).

Thanks —

Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — that recap is super helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we share data: 

1) Dataset format: can you confirm the exact schema for the metadata column? Our export pipeline is in Parquet; we can output CSV but prefer to minimize re-formatting.
2) PII: the alerts currently contain customer PII in the payload. Can you confirm Redwood's recommended anonymization pattern and whether the private VPC eval will accept encrypted PII (we'd prefer to keep data encrypted in transit and at rest under our KMS).
3) Gov/compliance: do you have a SOC 2 report we can send to procurement? They will also want a short statement on retention policy for eval data.

Also — Rishi, do you have a small script we can run that validates the CSV/JSONL format before upload? That would speed handoff.

Best,
Erin Walsh

Acme Bank

Hi Erin —

Short answers to your questions below: 

1) Metadata schema: recommended minimal fields (send as JSON-string in the metadata cell or separate CSV columns): {agent_id, source_type, event_timestamp, case_id}. If Parquet is easier, we can accept Parquet — we just need the same fields present. We included a small sample CSV (acme-eval-dataset-sample.csv) with this email.

2) PII / encryption: Private VPC eval is the recommended path if you want to keep data under your KMS. We can accept encrypted payloads and run the eval in an air-gapped VPC that uses your KMS keys for decryption (we do require a short onboarding checklist for the KMS handshake). For hosted sandbox runs, we have stricter redaction guidance — we generally recommend hashing or tokenizing direct identifiers prior to handoff.

3) Compliance docs: I attached our SOC 2 summary and the SLA/pricing PDF. Full SOC 2 audit report can be shared under NDA — procurement often requests that. Retention policy: eval inputs/results are retained by default for 30 days in hosted sandbox; for Private VPC we respect customer retention settings and can set immediate deletion post-run per contract.

Script & validation: Rishi — can you drop a small validator script and the redwood-eval-template.jsonl to make it easy for Erin's team? Ideally a tiny python script that validates required columns and flags PII fields.

If that all looks good Erin, can you confirm: (a) which hosting option you prefer, and (b) an initial data handoff ETA? We'll stand up a private VPC env within 24 hours of confirmation.

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Hi Erin —

Thanks — looping in a short technical checklist and a tiny validator you can run locally. Happy to walk through this on a 30-min call; please share a few windows and I will send a calendar invite.

Pre-reqs for Private VPC eval (if chosen):
- S3 bucket or secure FTP with a single upload path.
- KMS key details and contact for key handshake.
- List of models you want included in the run (we recommend +1 smaller, +1 baseline, +1 high-quality).

Validator (Python — run before upload):
# validate_eval.py
import csv, json, sys
req_cols = ["input", "reference", "metadata"]
with open(sys.argv[1], newline='') as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f)
    for i, row in enumerate(reader, 1):
        for c in req_cols:
            if c not in row or row[c] == '':
                print(f"Missing {c} at row {i}")
                sys.exit(2)
print('OK')

Evaluation run outline:
- Baseline run within 48 hours of data receipt (we'll run the three models Marissa suggested).
- We produce: per-example outputs, automated metric table, and human sample of 200 items with reviewer tags.
- Delivery: results deck + raw artifacts (CSV with model outputs) within 5 business days.

Timeline and next actions:
1) Erin: confirm hosted vs private and share data ETA.
2) Acme procurement: if private, we will exchange the onboarding checklist and SOC 2 NDA.
3) We'll schedule a 30-min tech call — propose Aug 16 or Aug 17 between 10-12 PT.
